# 30. Website Audit

<!-- Generated by tools/build_checklists.py. Edit the generator to change checklist structure. -->

**Purpose:** Evaluate existing or newly built static sites against premium quality standards and produce actionable, prioritized remediation.

## Universal Constraints
- [ ] The solution must remain static front-end only: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, documents, and generated static files only.
- [ ] The stack must avoid proprietary lock-in, paid builders, paid plugins, closed hosting features that cannot be replaced, and opaque third-party scripts where an open or free-tier-friendly alternative exists.
- [ ] Every decision must be documented as a quality rule, acceptance criterion, or exception with rationale; implementation notes belong outside the checklist.
- [ ] Every checklist item must be testable by review, automated audit, source inspection, browser testing, or client sign-off.
- [ ] Manual exceptions must record the owner, reason, expiration date, affected pages, and residual risk.

## Must Exist
- [ ] An audit scope defining URLs, templates, languages, devices, browsers, forms, analytics, and excluded areas.
- [ ] A severity model for critical, high, medium, low, and advisory findings.
- [ ] A scoring model that does not hide critical defects behind averages.
- [ ] Evidence for each finding: URL, screenshot or source reference, reproduction, impact, and recommended fix owner.
- [ ] A technical audit covering HTML, CSS, JS, SEO, accessibility, performance, security, assets, links, hosting, and analytics.
- [ ] A content and brand audit covering clarity, proof, consistency, claims, freshness, and conversion support.
- [ ] A compliance audit covering privacy, consent, legal pages, licensing, and jurisdiction-sensitive issues.
- [ ] A remediation roadmap separating quick fixes, structural fixes, content fixes, legal review, and future improvements.

## Must Be True
- [ ] Audit findings must be specific enough to act on.
- [ ] Critical accessibility, security, legal, form, and indexability issues must outrank cosmetic preferences.
- [ ] The audit must distinguish objective defects from strategic recommendations.
- [ ] Automated findings must be manually reviewed before client presentation.
- [ ] Scores must not imply compliance without appropriate manual review.
- [ ] The audit must respect static-site constraints and avoid recommending backend or paid-builder fixes unless explicitly scoped.
- [ ] Recommendations must prefer free, open-source, and portable methods.
- [ ] The final report must identify what automation can fix and what requires human judgment.

## Must Be Checked
- [ ] Check crawlability, metadata, headings, schema, sitemap, robots, canonicals, hreflang, and duplicate content.
- [ ] Check accessibility with automated tools and manual keyboard review.
- [ ] Check performance budgets, image sizes, Core Web Vitals risks, third-party scripts, and caching.
- [ ] Check forms, conversion paths, CTA clarity, trust signals, and post-submit states.
- [ ] Check privacy notices, tracking behavior, consent, external processors, and license records.
- [ ] Check hosting headers, HTTPS, redirects, exposed files, mixed content, and secret hygiene.
- [ ] Check local SEO, NAP, GBP alignment, location pages, and LocalBusiness schema where relevant.
- [ ] Check client maintainability, documentation, dependencies, and portability.

## Must Be Avoided
- [ ] Avoid presenting automated tool output as the audit itself.
- [ ] Avoid burying critical findings in long undifferentiated lists.
- [ ] Avoid recommendations that require paid plugins or proprietary rebuilds when static fixes are possible.
- [ ] Avoid style criticism without tying it to usability, brand, conversion, or accessibility impact.
- [ ] Avoid false certainty on legal compliance without legal review.
- [ ] Avoid changing production during audit unless explicitly approved.

## Premium Acceptance Standard
- [ ] The audit must make the next best action obvious.
- [ ] The report must be useful to business stakeholders and implementers.
- [ ] Findings must be prioritized by risk, impact, and effort.
- [ ] Audit tooling must be repeatable so improvements can be verified.

## Automation Hooks
- [ ] Use the Python audit script as the baseline static analyzer.
- [ ] Use the fix script only for safe, mechanical remediations; human review remains mandatory for strategy, content, legal, brand, and conversion judgments.

## Detailed Best-Practice Review Areas
- [ ] Audit covers UX, QA, SEO, analytics, tracking, accessibility, planning, hosting, development, CMS/export, security, DevOps, performance, monitoring, legal/privacy, assets, content, conversion, and launch readiness.
- [ ] Findings include severity, category, code, affected page/file, evidence, fixability, how-to-fix guidance, report date, and manual review requirements.
- [ ] Audit distinguishes safe mechanical fixes from human judgment areas such as brand, strategy, legal, accessibility conformance, visual polish, claim truth, and conversion quality.
- [ ] Reports prioritize critical/high launch blockers first, then medium quality issues, then low polish/maintenance improvements.

## Report Output Required
- [ ] Report every failed automated check with severity, checklist category, issue code, affected file or page, evidence, whether it is script-fixable, and how to fix it.
- [ ] Report every manual-only failure with reviewer, affected page or component, expected standard, actual behavior, recommended fix, owner, and target date.
- [ ] Separate launch blockers from quality improvements so critical static-site failures cannot be hidden by low-priority polish notes.
- [ ] Attach the JSON audit report, Markdown audit report, screenshots where visual proof is needed, and manual QA evidence for browser, device, keyboard, screen reader, form, analytics, and live deployment checks.

## Evidence Required
- [ ] Record reviewed pages, tools used, dates, reviewers, unresolved exceptions, and links to generated reports.
- [ ] Attach screenshots or source references for failures that cannot be proven by automated reports.
- [ ] Mark checklist items as complete only when the production static output satisfies the rule.
